chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

O Is'haq! Do not count as a calamity one upon which you are granted patience and have thereby obligated for yourself from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, the reward; rather, the calamity is that from which its owner is deprived of its reward and recompense when he does not exercise patience at its occurrence.
ai.seo_question: What defines a true calamity in Shia theology according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the event of calamity and the spiritual state of the believer, asserting that true loss occurs only when one fails to maintain patience (sabr) at the moment of occurrence, thereby forfeiting the promised reward. This hadith, found in al-Kafi’s chapter on patience, underscores the Shia emphasis on active spiritual vigilance, where the quality of one's response determines whether a trial becomes a means of elevation or a source of deprivation. It reinforces the principle that divine decree is not merely an external occurrence but an internal test of faith that yields recompense contingent upon the believer's conscious endurance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Muhammad Bin yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘O Is’haq! Do not count it as a difficulty upon which patience comes upon it and it Obligates the Reward from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon it, but rather, the difficulty is that which deprives its owner from its Recompense when he does not observe patience during its descent’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that, O Ishaq, do not count a misfortune in which you were granted patience, thus you deserved reward from Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious. A misfortune is that in which due to acting impatiently, one is deprived of rewards for that suffering.”
